ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.method: A STRUCTURAL sweep over the tracked tree, distinguishing an ALLOCATION POSITION from a mere literal occurrence. An allocation position is a parsed-JSON member whose KEY is one of GRANT_ID, authorityId, grant_id, authority_id, version or artifact_id, and whose VALUE matches the candidate EXACTLY - never a substring in prose, never a bare array element. A FIXED-STRING containment sweep over raw bytes was run alongside it, and every literal hit was classified by reading its containing clause.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_two_sweeps_are_both_needed: A value-exact sweep that ignored key position would count prohibition-list array elements as allocations. A key-position sweep alone would report ZERO and prove nothing about whether the id is discussed elsewhere. Reporting both, and classifying every literal, is what makes the negative non-vacuous.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_FIXED_STRING_and_not_regex: git grep treats '.' as a wildcard, so a regex search for a dotted version string can match unrelated digits separated by any character and manufacture a phantom hit. v1.0.32 disclosed exactly such a false positive for its own candidate.
